ko.label: Capital controls on personal wealth
ko.explanation: IMF lists CFMs on "suspension/limitation of outward remittances on capital transactions made by residents" and on emigrants' outward transfers (eased since 2024); CBSL Direction 16 of 2021 lets a Non-National resident or non-resident remit only "USD 30,000 per annum" out of the capital proceeds (investment/property) credited to a Capital Transactions Rupee Account (superannuation is uncapped). Direction is 2021; amendments after that not checked.

data.name: Sri Lanka
data.summary: Sri Lanka taxes residents on worldwide income at 6%-36% from April 2025. Capital gains on investment assets, including foreign shares, are taxed at 15% from 3 June 2026 (previously 10%); Colombo-listed shares and the main home are excluded. Sri Lankan dividends bear a 15% final withholding tax. Foreign income remitted through a bank in foreign currency is capped at 15%, but foreign income kept abroad is taxed at slab rates. There is no inheritance, gift or wealth tax, and death does not trigger capital gains tax.

regimes.name: Sri Lankan tax resident
regimes.description: Worldwide income at 6%-36%; 15% capital gains tax on investment assets; 15% final WHT on Sri Lankan dividends.
regimes.eligibility: Resident for a year of assessment (1 April-31 March) if residing in Sri Lanka or present 183 days or more in any 12-month period that starts or ends in the year (s. 69).

capital_gains.summary: Residents are taxed on worldwide income. Gains from realising 'investment assets' (land and buildings, shares and other securities, membership interests) are taxed separately: individuals paid 10%, raised to 15% from 3 June 2026 by Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act No. 11 of 2026 (First Schedule para. 1(2)(a)). Shares quoted on the Colombo Stock Exchange and the principal residence (owned 3 years, lived in 2) are excluded. Small gains (each up to LKR 50,000, total up to LKR 600,000 a year) are exempt.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: CSE-quoted shares excluded; principal residence excluded; resident individual's gains exempt if each gain is LKR 50,000 or less and total gains are LKR 600,000 or less in the year. Cost of assets held on 30 September 2017 = market value then.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: The IRD CGT page (updated 19 November 2025) still shows 10% for non-companies; the June 2026 Act raises it to 15% from the date it became law. Capital losses are not deductible against gains (IRD). Transfers on death and gifts to close relatives carry over cost (no deemed gain; ss. 45-46).

sources.title: Inland Revenue (Amendment) Act, No. 11 of 2026 (certified 3 June 2026)
Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017 - consolidated text with 2025 changes

capital_gains.rate_basis: 15% CGT on gains from realisation of investment assets for individuals from 3 June 2026 (Act No. 11 of 2026, s. 36(1)); CSE-quoted shares excluded (0). Foreign shares and foreign property are investment assets of a resident taxed on worldwide income.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Shares or land held as trading stock are business income at slab rates up to 36%.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation with a foreign tax credit (ss. 80-81). From 1 April 2025, foreign-source gains and profits earned in foreign currency and remitted through a bank to Sri Lanka are capped at 15% (Act No. 2 of 2025).

dividends.summary: Dividends paid by a Sri Lankan resident company bear 15% withholding tax, which is a final withholding payment since 1 January 2023 (s. 88(1A)(aa)). Foreign dividends of a resident are taxable investment income at the progressive rates (6%-36% from 1 April 2025) with a foreign tax credit, but foreign-source income earned in foreign currency and remitted through a bank to Sri Lanka is taxed at no more than 15% from 1 April 2025.
dividends.important_exceptions: Before 1 April 2025 remitted foreign-source income was exempt; it now bears up to 15%. Foreign income not remitted is taxed at the ordinary rates.

sources.title: Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017 - consolidated text with 2025 changes

open_questions: Whether investment income from foreign portfolios kept abroad is in practice taxed at 36% or can be structured into the 15% cap through remittance was not explored.
dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 15% final WHT. Foreign: top slab 36% (taxable income above LKR 2.5 million) before credit, assuming the dividends are not remitted; if remitted via a bank in foreign currency the cap is 15%.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% WHT on dividends, final for non-residents too (s. 88(1A)), reducible by treaty.
dividends.treaty_network: About 45 DTAs including the US, UK and several EU states (count from general knowledge, not verified).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 30% from 1 April 2025 (First Schedule para. 4); remitted foreign-source profits of companies 15%.

sources.title: Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017 - consolidated text with 2025 changes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Local authority rates on property; stamp duty on land transfers; restrictions on foreigners owning land (condominium units allowed; not verified).

inheritance.summary: Sri Lanka has no inheritance, estate or gift tax. The Inland Revenue Act treats an asset passing on death as realised at its net cost, with the heir taking that cost (s. 45), so death triggers no capital gains tax. Gifts to a child, spouse, parent and other close relatives are likewise realised at cost under conditions (s. 46(2)-(3)). Stamp duty applies to deeds transferring Sri Lankan land (not verified).

sources.title: Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017 - consolidated text with 2025 changes

open_questions: IMF-programme discussions in 2023-2025 mentioned introducing wealth or inheritance taxation; nothing was found in the 2025-2026 amending Acts.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax. Gifts of investment assets to close relatives roll over at cost (s. 46); other gifts are deemed realised at market value for CGT.

residency.tax_residency_test: Year of assessment 1 April-31 March. Resident if residing in Sri Lanka or present 183 days or more in any 12-month period commencing or ending in the year (Inland Revenue Act s. 69).

routes.name: Residence visas (investor, retiree, 'Golden Paradise' visa)
routes.requirements: Sri Lanka offers long-term residence visas against foreign-currency deposits or investment (amounts and current terms not verified).

corporate.summary: Standard company rate 30% from 1 April 2025; 15% on remitted foreign-source profits and export services; 45% for betting/gaming and liquor/tobacco (Act No. 2 of 2025).
